source: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/9143-2025-A-Updated and C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/9143-2025-B-Updated (FRC team 9143, two sibling 2025 Reefscape robots, both updated to 2026 deps)
summary: These are two well-written, heavily-commented, plain-WPILib command-based robots (no AdvantageKit IO layers, no replay) that share an enormous amount of literally copy-pasted infrastructure. Swerve.java (500 lines) is byte-identical between the two robots except for ONE comment line; Telemetry.java, LimelightHelpers.java (1946 lines), util/Elastic.java (390 lines), Main.java, build.gradle, gradle.properties, .vscode/settings.json, RobotContainerTest.java and ChoreoTrajectoryTest.java are all 100% identical; Vision.java differs only in the goal-resolver body; Robot.java differs by 19 lines (mostly the log metadata string); RobotContainer.java shares ~180 identical lines of drive requests, D-pad nudges, SysId bindings, Choreo auto discovery, and vision toggle. Architecture is: one god `Constants.java` of nested `public static final class XConstants` with a hand-maintained CAN ID map in the header comment, CTRE Tuner-X-generated `TunerConstants.java` for swerve, subsystems that own hardware directly and expose plain getters, a central `Dashboard.java` that is the *only* NetworkTables publisher, and (in A only) a `Superstructure.java` command-factory motion planner with collision interlocks. Every gain, limit, preset, and sim constant is a hardcoded `public static final double` — there is not a single tunable number, `Preferences` call, or `SmartDashboard.getNumber` anywhere in either repo; tuning is done by editing Java and redeploying, or via REV Hardware Client / Tuner X. Simulation is hand-wired per subsystem (`ElevatorSim`, `SingleJointedArmSim`, `SparkMaxSim`, TalonFX `getSimState()`) with the same ~15-line `simulationPeriodic()` shape repeated. Logging is AdvantageKit `LoggedRobot` + `WPILOGWriter` + `RLOGServer(5810)` with all `Logger.recordOutput` calls funneled through `Dashboard.update()`. The repos are NOT thin and are NOT vendor boilerplate — they represent a mature, opinionated house style with real hard-won knowledge (FPGA→Phoenix timestamp conversion, MegaTag1-while-disabled heading seeding, non-blocking `setPosition(x, 0)`, spin-based vision rejection) that is currently trapped in copy-paste.
stack: WPILib 2026 / GradleRIO 2026.2.1, Java 17 (`sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17`), Gradle pinned to `org.gradle.java.home=C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026/jdk` via gradle.properties. Vendordeps (identical version-for-version in both repos): Phoenix6 26.3.0, REVLib 2026.0.5, PathplannerLib 2026.1.2, AdvantageKit 26.0.2, WPILibNewCommands 1.0.0. LimelightHelpers v1.14 vendored as source (requires LLOS 2026.0+). Elastic dashboard via vendored `util/Elastic.java` (Gold87 ElasticLib) + `deploy/elastic-layout.json` served over `WebServer.start(5800, ...)`. Motor controllers: Kraken X60 / TalonFX (swerve drive+steer, A's CorAl pivot+intake), NEO on Spark MAX (A's elevator x2, B's KitBot roller, B's AlLow pivot+roller). Sensors: CANcoder x4, Pigeon 2 (id 2), CTRE CANrange (A, game piece), REV Through Bore absolute encoder on DIO 0 (A, pivot), CTRE CANdle (A, LEDs, id 5), 3x Limelight (A: funnel/barge/reef; B: zero cameras, stack inert). Autonomous: PathPlanner AutoBuilder + Choreo `.traj` loaded through `PathPlannerPath.fromChoreoTrajectory` (ChoreoLib deliberately NOT used - no 2026 release). Testing: JUnit 5 (5.10.1) with `forkEvery = 1` because simulated CAN devices reject duplicate IDs in one JVM. NOTE: `settings.gradle` disagrees between repos — A has `String frcYear = '2025'`, B has `'2026'`, while both `.wpilib/wpilib_preferences.json` say `"projectYear": "2026"`.

patterns.name: Swerve subsystem wrapper over CTRE TunerSwerveDrivetrain (THE strongest duplication signal)
patterns.whatItDoes: Extends the Tuner-X-generated `TunerSwerveDrivetrain` and implements `Subsystem`, layering on: three duplicated constructors that each repeat `new Vision(this)` + `startSimThread()` + `createAprilTagTrackingCommand()` + `configureAutoBuilder()`; PathPlanner AutoBuilder wiring with `RobotConfig.fromGUISettings()` in a try/catch; `applyRequest(Supplier<SwerveRequest>)`; three SysId routines (translation/steer/rotation) with a `setSysIdRoutine(SysIdRoutineType)` selector; alliance-aware operator perspective in `periodic()`; a 5 ms `Notifier` sim thread; and an overridden `addVisionMeasurement` doing FPGA→Phoenix timebase conversion plus spin-based rejection.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/9143-2025-A-Updated/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/Swerve.java (500 lines) and C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/9143-2025-B-Updated/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/Swerve.java (499 lines) — `diff --strip-trailing-cr` reports exactly 3 differing lines, all inside one Javadoc sentence.
patterns.libraryValue: This is 500 lines of nontrivial, correctness-critical code duplicated verbatim across two robots. It should be Rootstock's flagship class: a `RootstockSwerve` base that takes drivetrain constants + a path-following gain record + a vision-goal strategy, exposing the SysId routines, AutoBuilder config, operator perspective, and the timestamp/spin-rejection logic for free. The two robot-specific deltas (auto PID gains, vision goal resolver) are exactly the injection points.

patterns.name: Centralized Dashboard publisher (subsystems publish nothing)
patterns.whatItDoes: A single non-Subsystem `Dashboard` class constructed in RobotContainer and pumped once per loop from `Robot.robotPeriodic()` via `m_robotContainer.updateDashboard()`. It owns: `Field2d`, the Elastic `SwerveDrive` widget (raw NT subtable with a `.type` marker and 9 cached `NetworkTableEntry`s), `Mechanism2d` schematics, `Pose3d[]` component poses for AdvantageScope, every `SmartDashboard.putX` call, every `Logger.recordOutput` call, and every WPILib `Alert`. Every subsystem carries the identical Javadoc line: "Dashboard note: this subsystem publishes nothing itself."
patterns.whereSeen: A: .../frc/robot/Dashboard.java (332 lines); B: .../frc/robot/Dashboard.java (235 lines). ~90 lines are character-identical (swerve widget setup, vitals block, alliance/battery alert, vision block).
patterns.libraryValue: The *shape* is excellent and should be preserved, but the mechanical parts are pure boilerplate: the Elastic SwerveDrive widget setup, the drivetrain vitals block (Speed/Heading/Match Time/Battery/CAN Utilization), the low-battery alert, and the vision has-target key precomputation are identical. Rootstock should ship `RootstockDashboard` with pluggable "panels" so a robot only writes its own mechanism block, plus a declarative `Alert` helper (condition supplier + message + one-shot Elastic toast on rising edge) — A hand-rolls that toast latch with a `throughBoreWasConnected` boolean.

patterns.name: Choreo-trajectory auto discovery folded into the PathPlanner chooser
patterns.whatItDoes: `addChoreoAutos()` scans `Filesystem.getDeployDirectory()/choreo` for `*.traj`, sorts them, loads each via `PathPlannerPath.fromChoreoTrajectory(name)`, and adds it to the same `LoggedDashboardChooser` as `"Choreo: <name>"`. `choreoAutoCommand(path)` resets odometry to the trajectory's start pose, alliance-flipping it with `AutoBuilder.shouldFlip() ? FlippingUtil.flipFieldPose(start) : start`, then follows. A malformed file is reported via `DriverStation.reportError` and skipped rather than crashing construction.
patterns.whereSeen: A: RobotContainer.java lines 335-367; B: RobotContainer.java lines 308-340. Byte-identical including the 15-line Javadoc explaining why ChoreoLib is not used.
patterns.libraryValue: Genuinely reusable, non-obvious, and already battle-tested (there's a dedicated `ChoreoTrajectoryTest` in both repos, also identical). Should be a one-liner in Rootstock: `RootstockAuto.addChoreoTrajectories(chooser, drivetrain)`.

patterns.name: Multi-Limelight MegaTag1/MegaTag2 pose fusion with disabled-time heading seeding
patterns.whatItDoes: Per loop: pushes gyro heading to every camera with `SetRobotOrientation_NoFlush` (one `LimelightHelpers.Flush()` after the loop instead of per-camera), then chooses MegaTag1 while DISABLED (so its absolute heading solve seeds the gyro) and MegaTag2 while enabled. Std devs are computed as `xyStdDev = 0.3 + 0.4*avgTagDist^2 / max(1, tagCount)` and `rotStdDev = disabled ? (tagCount>=2 ? 0.3 : 0.9) : 9999999`. Also caches a `findBestTarget()` result once per `periodic()` so dashboard + tracking command share one NT read.
patterns.whereSeen: A: subsystems/Vision.java lines 320-363; B: subsystems/Vision.java (same block, character-identical). The whole `updateRobotPosition()` method, the `AprilTagTarget`/`TrackingGoal` value classes, `isReefTag`/`isCoralStationTag` linear scans, `toggleTracking`, `hasTarget(int)`, and the precomputed `limelightTableNames` array are all duplicated.
patterns.libraryValue: This is the single hardest-to-get-right piece of FRC vision code and it is copy-pasted. Rootstock should own it as `RootstockVision`: a camera list (name + facing sign), a std-dev policy interface, and the MegaTag1-while-disabled seeding baked in. Only the goal resolver differs between robots (A resolves per superstructure goal + branch side; B returns flush-and-centered), which is exactly a strategy/functional-interface seam.

patterns.name: "Positional mechanism with latched setpoint + manual override that holds on release"
patterns.whatItDoes: The same subsystem skeleton appears three times across the two repos (A's Elevator on Spark MAX MAXMotion, A's CorAl pivot on TalonFX Motion Magic, B's AlLow pivot on Spark MAX position control). Every one has: `private double target; private boolean manualModeEnabled; private boolean positionControlEnabled;`, a `setPosition/setPivotAngle` that clamps to MIN/MAX and flips the two booleans, a `holdCurrentPosition()/holdCurrentAngle()` that calls set(get()), a `manualControl(stick)` that applies a deadband + speed limit and captures-and-holds on release, an `isAtTarget()` using an ALLOWED_ERROR constant, a `stopX()` that drops the closed loop, a `resetEncoder()`, and 4 diagnostic getters (`getXCurrent`, `getXOutput`).
patterns.libraryValue: This is the highest-leverage mechanism abstraction in the codebase. Rootstock should provide a `PositionMechanism` base (or a composable `SetpointHolder` + `ManualOverride` pair) parameterized by a motor-controller adapter, so a new elevator/arm/pivot is ~30 lines of config instead of ~250 lines of near-identical state machine. The three-boolean state (`manualModeEnabled` / `positionControlEnabled` / implicit "neither") is exactly the kind of hand-rolled state that a library enum should own.

patterns.name: Superstructure: deferred, state-gated collision-avoidance motion planner (A only)
patterns.whatItDoes: A non-Subsystem command factory that owns ALL coordinated elevator+arm motion. `moveTo()` wraps `Commands.defer(() -> planMove(h, a), Set.of(elevator, coral))` so the plan is built from REAL mechanism state at button-press time. `planMove` has three cases (low-box direct / tuck-from-low-box / general), and the general path is `escapeCurrentPose(...).andThen(travelAndFinish(...))`. Overlaps are gated on measured position (`Commands.waitUntil(() -> elevator.getCurrentPosition() >= handoff)`), never on timing. The ascending escape re-evaluates its ceiling every loop so the elevator target ratchets up as the arm swings, avoiding stop-and-go stutter. A `Goal` enum records the last commanded pose family and is handed to Vision via `swerve.getVision().setGoalSupplier(superstructure::getGoal)`.
patterns.libraryValue: Not directly shareable (the geometry is robot-specific), but the *pattern* absolutely is: deferred planning from live state, measured-state gates rather than timeouts, a `settle()` helper with a timeout on the final wait only, and `handleInterrupt(stopRollers)` on every roller command. Rootstock should ship the scaffolding — a `Superstructure<G extends Enum<G>>` base with `defer`-based `moveTo`, a `settle(timeout)` helper, and a goal-enum → vision-goal supplier bridge — plus a documented "safe region" declaration API so teams describe forbidden (height, angle) zones instead of hand-writing the branch tree.

patterns.name: Preset enum with a single `double` payload
patterns.whatItDoes: Every mechanism's setpoints are a nested enum carrying one primitive: `PresetHeights.CORAL_L4(52.5).getHeight()`, `PivotPresetAngles.RAISE(90.0).getAngle()`, B's `AlLowConstants.PivotPresetAngles.INTAKE(45.0).getAngle()`. Each enum re-declares the same private field + constructor + getter boilerplate.
patterns.libraryValue: The idea is right (named, self-documenting setpoints beat magic numbers at call sites), but the 8-line boilerplate is re-typed per enum, the getters have inconsistent names (`getHeight` vs `getAngle`), and the values are raw doubles with the unit only in a comment. Rootstock should offer a `Setpoint` interface (`double value()`) or unit-typed presets (`Distance`/`Angle` from `edu.wpi.first.units`) so presets are dimension-checked — the author already imports `edu.wpi.first.units.Units.*` in TunerConstants and clearly likes units.

patterns.name: Derived-gearing constants written as visible tooth-count arithmetic
patterns.whatItDoes: Gear ratios are never written as a magic decimal; they are written as the multiplication of real tooth counts with the power path spelled out in the comment above. This is the single best habit in the codebase.
patterns.whereSeen: A/Constants.java line 59 `ELEVATOR_GEAR_RATIO = 5.0 * 3.0 * 3.0`, line 64 `ELEVATOR_SPROCKET_CIRCUMFERENCE = 22 * 0.25`, line 74 `ELEVATOR_INCHES_PER_ROTATION = SPROCKET_CIRCUMFERENCE * CASCADE_RATIO / GEAR_RATIO`, line 173 `CORAL_PIVOT_GEAR_RATIO = (58.0/10.0) * (58.0/18.0) * (42.0/12.0)`; A/TunerConstants.java line 107 `kCoupleRatio = 50.0 / 16.0`.
patterns.libraryValue: Rootstock should formalize this as a tiny `Gearing`/`Reduction` builder (`Reduction.of(58,10).then(58,18).then(42,12)` → `.ratio()`), plus `Conversions` helpers for sprocket-pitch-to-linear and cascade multipliers. It makes the good habit cheap and makes the derivation machine-checkable rather than comment-checkable. Contrast with B's AlLow, where the author had to *reverse-engineer* the ratio: `ALLOW_PIVOT_POSITION_CONVERSION = 13.334; // 13.334 deg/rot implies a ~27:1 reduction (360 / 13.334). VERIFY` — exactly the failure this abstraction prevents.

patterns.name: KitBot command-factory subsystem (startEnd + withTimeout + withName)
patterns.whatItDoes: A roller subsystem that exposes ONLY command factories, never raw setters. Each is `startEnd(() -> motor.set(SPEED), motor::stopMotor).withTimeout(D).withName("X")`. The same factories are consumed by both button bindings and PathPlanner `NamedCommands.registerCommand(...)`, so there is exactly one definition of "eject".
patterns.whereSeen: B/.../subsystems/KitBot.java lines 55-86; registered in B/RobotContainer.java lines 118-121.
patterns.libraryValue: This is the cleanest subsystem in either repo and the pattern the others should follow (A's CorAl exposes raw `setIntakeSpeed` and the Superstructure must manually add `.handleInterrupt(coral::stopIntake)` to four separate commands). Rootstock should ship a `RollerSubsystem` with `runAt(speed)`, `runFor(speed, duration)`, and automatic stop-on-end, plus a helper that registers a map of NamedCommands so the string names can't drift from the .auto files.

patterns.name: State-derived LED subsystem with change-detection (A only)
patterns.whatItDoes: A CANdle subsystem driven entirely by `BooleanSupplier`s injected at construction (`new LEDs(coral::isGamePieceDetected, swerve::isVisionTrackingEnabled)`). `computeState()` returns an `LEDState` from a fixed priority ladder; `periodic()` only calls `applyState()` when the state changes OR when the alliance color changes underneath an alliance-colored state. Control requests are allocated once and reused; a `clearAnimationRequest` (EmptyAnimation slot 0) is sent before any solid color.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/9143-2025-A-Updated/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/LEDs.java (195 lines). B has no LEDs at all.
patterns.libraryValue: Highly generalizable and a common team need. Rootstock should offer `PrioritizedLeds`: register `(BooleanSupplier condition, Pattern pattern)` pairs in priority order, get the change-detection, the late-alliance re-apply, and the animation-slot clearing for free. The alliance-late-report bug (`displayedAllianceColor` re-apply) is exactly the kind of hard-won detail a library should encode once.

patterns.name: Hand-wired per-subsystem physics simulation
patterns.whatItDoes: Each positional subsystem constructs its sim plant behind `if (RobotBase.isSimulation())` and implements `simulationPeriodic()` with the same 3-step shape: read the sim motor's applied output → drive the WPILib plant with `update(0.02)` → feed the resulting velocity/position back into the simulated encoder. Spark MAX uses `SparkMaxSim.iterate(vel, RobotController.getBatteryVoltage(), 0.02)`; TalonFX uses `getSimState().setRawRotorPosition(rot * gearRatio)` / `setRotorVelocity(...)`.
patterns.whereSeen: A/Elevator.java lines 88-99 + 287-296; A/CorAl.java lines 104-114 + 417-429; B/AlLow.java lines 93-104 + 310-319.
patterns.libraryValue: The `0.02` timestep is hardcoded in all five places, the sim mass/length estimates are private static finals scattered per file, and the TalonFX gear-ratio multiplication is easy to get backwards. Rootstock should provide `SimHarness` adapters (`SparkSim.attach(plant, encoderScale)` / `TalonFxSim.attach(plant, sensorToMechanismRatio)`) that own the timestep and the unit conversion, so a subsystem declares a plant and gets sim for free. Also worth encoding: A's Elevator models the cascade as an effective drum radius `Units.inchesToMeters(11.0) / (2.0 * Math.PI)` — a nonobvious trick.

patterns.name: Elastic dashboard tab auto-switching on mode change + one-shot toast notifications
patterns.whatItDoes: `Robot.disabledInit/autonomousInit/teleopInit/testInit` each call `Elastic.selectTab("Setup"/"Autonomous"/"Teleop"/"Testing")`, and `WebServer.start(5800, Filesystem.getDeployDirectory().getPath())` serves `deploy/elastic-layout.json` so every drive-station laptop loads the identical layout via Ctrl+D. `Elastic.sendNotification(...)` fires a toast on a rising-edge failure.
patterns.whereSeen: A/Robot.java lines 62, 93, 108, 126, 142; A/Dashboard.java lines 324-330; vendored util/Elastic.java (390 lines, identical in both repos).
patterns.libraryValue: The `Elastic.java` helper is a vendored third-party file duplicated byte-for-byte — Rootstock should just own it (or depend on it) so it's updated in one place. The mode→tab mapping and the deploy-dir WebServer line are pure boilerplate that belongs in a `RootstockRobot` base class.
patterns.codeSketch:
WebServer.start(5800, Filesystem.getDeployDirectory().getPath());
@Override public void teleopInit() { Elastic.selectTab("Teleop"); if (m_autonomousCommand != null) m_autonomousCommand.cancel(); }

patterns.name: Robot bring-up boilerplate: AdvantageKit + PathPlanner warmup + disabledInit stop-everything
patterns.whatItDoes: The `Robot` constructor does `Logger.recordMetadata(...)`, `Logger.addDataReceiver(new WPILOGWriter())`, `Logger.addDataReceiver(new RLOGServer(5810))`, `Logger.start()`, starts the deploy WebServer, constructs RobotContainer, then `CommandScheduler.getInstance().schedule(FollowPathCommand.warmupCommand())` to avoid the first-path JIT stutter. `RobotContainer.disabledInit()` manually calls stop on every mechanism.
patterns.whereSeen: A/Robot.java lines 44-71 and 369-374 of RobotContainer.java; B/Robot.java lines 44-70 and 343-347 of RobotContainer.java. Differ only in the two metadata strings, one `CameraServer.startAutomaticCapture()` (B), and one `DriverStation.silenceJoystickConnectionWarning(true)` (A).
patterns.libraryValue: A `RootstockRobot extends LoggedRobot` base could take a project name + robot name and do all of it, including the RLOG-on-5810-because-5800-is-taken detail (a real, documented gotcha). `disabledInit()` stop-everything should be a registry (`Rootstock.onDisable(subsystem::stop)`) rather than a hand-maintained list that silently rots when a subsystem is added.

patterns.name: Reusable, pre-allocated swerve requests + identical driver binding block
patterns.whatItDoes: Four `SwerveRequest` fields (`FieldCentric drive`, `SwerveDriveBrake brake`, `PointWheelsAt point`, `RobotCentric forwardStraight`) allocated once with `.withDriveRequestType(DriveRequestType.Velocity)` and a 20% deadband, then bound: A=brake, B=point-at-stick, four D-pad `whileTrue` nudges at ±0.5 m/s, four back/start + X/Y SysId combos, left-bumper `seedFieldCentric()`, and the Y-toggle for vision tracking keyed off `aprilTagTrackingCommand.isScheduled()`.
patterns.whereSeen: A/RobotContainer.java lines 96-106 + 180-253; B/RobotContainer.java lines 80-90 + 154-224. Identical except the translation scale (A `* 0.25` for driver practice, B `* 0.75`) and B wrapping the Y-toggle in `if (VisionConstants.LIMELIGHT_NAMES.length > 0)`.
patterns.libraryValue: ~90 lines of identical binding code. Rootstock should offer a `DriverBindings.standard(controller, swerve, config)` that installs the whole default set with a configurable translation scale and nudge speed, so a robot's RobotContainer only contains what is actually robot-specific. The `isScheduled()`-based toggle with `finallyDo` cleanup is a genuinely good pattern worth encoding as `Trigger.toggleCommand(cmd)`.

patterns.name: Absolute-encoder-as-truth with guarded re-seeding of the motor sensor (A only)
patterns.whatItDoes: The REV Through Bore (read as a raw `DutyCycle` on DIO 0) is the angle reference. The TalonFX rotor is seeded from it at startup, again immediately before every `setPivotAngle` move, and re-synced from `periodic()` ONLY when neither position nor manual control is active (re-seeding mid-move shifts the reference frame and makes the arm land off target). Connection is detected via `throughBore.getFrequency() > 0` with automatic fallback to the motor sensor. The offset delta is wrapped with `delta -= range * Math.round(delta / range)` so it is stateless and safe for multiple readers.
patterns.libraryValue: A textbook `AbsoluteEncoderReference` abstraction: takes an absolute source + a motor sensor, exposes `angle()`, `isConnected()`, `isConsistent()`, and does the guarded re-seed automatically. The non-blocking `pivotMotor.setPosition(x, 0)` detail (the default overload BLOCKS the main loop up to 100 ms waiting for a CAN ack) is a serious footgun the author had to discover and comment — a library must encode it so nobody rediscovers it.

painPoints.problem: Swerve.java is 500 lines of correctness-critical code copy-pasted between two robots with a 3-line diff — and that diff is entirely inside a comment.
painPoints.evidence: `diff --strip-trailing-cr A/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/Swerve.java B/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/Swerve.java` → 3 lines, all in the `createAprilTagTrackingCommand` Javadoc ('the tag's class, the superstructure's goal, and the selected reef branch side' vs 'the tag's class'). Every SysId routine, the AutoBuilder try/catch, the sim Notifier, the operator-perspective logic, and the FPGA→Phoenix conversion exist twice on disk.
painPoints.libraryFix: Rootstock owns `RootstockSwerve` (extends the Tuner-generated drivetrain, implements Subsystem). Robot repos keep only TunerConstants.java (their real per-robot hardware) and pass in path-following gains + a vision goal strategy. Any future bugfix to timestamp handling or vision rejection lands in one place instead of N.

painPoints.problem: The same fix must be applied N times, and demonstrably already has drifted.
painPoints.evidence: Concrete drift found: `settings.gradle` says `String frcYear = '2025'` in A but `'2026'` in B, while both `.wpilib/wpilib_preferences.json` say `"projectYear": "2026"`. `Robot.java` has `DriverStation.silenceJoystickConnectionWarning(true)` in A but not B. A's `Dashboard` has 4 WPILib `Alert`s (through-bore, elevator sync, coral feedback, low battery); B has only the low-battery one — the shared vitals monitoring silently diverged. A's TunerConstants drive stator limit is `Amps.of(90)`, B's is `Amps.of(60)`, but B's `deploy/pathplanner/settings.json` declares `"driveCurrentLimit": 100.0`.
painPoints.libraryFix: Move the shared surface (Swerve, Vision, Telemetry, Elastic, Dashboard scaffolding, build/gradle conventions) into a versioned Rootstock dependency so 'update once' is literally true, and provide a single source of truth for chassis constants that both the code and a PathPlanner-settings exporter read.

painPoints.problem: There is not one tunable number in either repo — every gain, limit, and setpoint requires a code edit + redeploy to change.
painPoints.evidence: `grep -rn "Preferences|getNumber(|LoggedNetworkNumber|LoggedDashboardNumber|TunableNumber|SmartDashboard.getNumber"` across both `src` trees returns ZERO hits outside LimelightHelpers. Every gain is a `public static final double` (e.g. `ELEVATOR_kP = 0.4`, `CORAL_PIVOT_kP = 40.0`, `TRANSLATION_kP = 5.0` in A vs `10.0` in B). The A README's tuning procedure is prose in a Javadoc: 'TUNE - first power-on procedure: 1. Sanity-check the height reading... 2. Raise kG until the carriage just holds... 3. Command a preset and raise kP'. The tuning loop today is: edit Java → `./gradlew deploy` → retest, or leave the code and tune in REV Hardware Client / Tuner X (where the value then disagrees with the committed constant).
painPoints.libraryFix: A `TunableNumber` (LoggedNetworkNumber-backed, no-op-to-constant when not in tuning mode) is the single highest-value thing Rootstock can ship for this team. Pair it with a `GainsGroup` that pushes changed values to the controller on change, so the documented three-step procedures become live dashboard sliders instead of edit-deploy cycles.

painPoints.problem: Gains, IDs, and gearing are untyped `double`/`int` with units only in comments — dimensional errors are invisible to the compiler and one class of them is already commented as a hazard.
painPoints.evidence: A/Constants.java carries the convention 'Every value carries its unit in the comment (inches, degrees, amps, ...)', but the values are bare doubles. The degree↔rotation conversion is then done by hand at every Phoenix call site with a literal `/ 360.0`: `config.MotionMagic.MotionMagicCruiseVelocity = CORAL_PIVOT_MAX_VELOCITY / 360.0;`, `config.SoftwareLimitSwitch.ForwardSoftLimitThreshold = CORAL_PIVOT_MAX_ANGLE / 360.0;`, `pivotMotor.setControl(positionRequest.withPosition(targetAngle / 360.0))`, `getMotorAngle() { return pivotMotor.getPosition().getValueAsDouble() * 360.0; }` — nine separate hand-written `/360` or `*360` in CorAl.java alone. CorAl.java even needs a warning comment: '(Phoenix divides rotor rotations by this ratio; do NOT put a rotations-to-degrees multiplier here.)'
painPoints.libraryFix: Use `edu.wpi.first.units` types (`Angle`, `Distance`, `LinearVelocity`) in Rootstock's public API — the author already uses them comfortably in TunerConstants (`Amps.of(120.0)`, `Inches.of(2)`, `MetersPerSecond.of(5.96)`). A `MechanismAngle` wrapper that owns the rotations↔degrees boundary would delete every `/360.0` and make the 'do NOT multiply here' comment unnecessary.

painPoints.problem: CAN ID maps and pin maps are maintained as ASCII-art comments with no compile-time or runtime validation, and this has already caused a robot-code crash.
painPoints.evidence: A/Constants.java header comment is a hand-drawn 'CAN ID MAP' table; the code below it carries `// VERIFY: this was previously documented/configured as 64, but Phoenix device IDs only go up to 62 - constructing a device with ID 64 throws and crashes robot code on boot (caught by RobotContainerTest).` The A README elevates this to checklist item 6a. The comment map also has a stale entry: '(63 is free - previously reserved for the removed AlLow mechanism)'. Meanwhile B uses CAN id 5 for a KitBot Spark MAX while A uses CAN id 5 for the CANdle — the same number, different meaning, tracked only in prose.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `CanId` value type with range validation (Phoenix 0-62, REV 1-62) that fails fast with a readable message at construction, plus a `DeviceRegistry` that detects duplicate-ID registration within a robot and can emit the CAN map as a logged artifact instead of a comment that rots.

painPoints.problem: Constants.java is a single monolithic file mixing per-robot hardware IDs, physical geometry, tuning gains, field-layout knowledge, and logging array indices — and the field knowledge is duplicated across robots.
painPoints.evidence: A/Constants.java is 448 lines containing ElevatorConstants, CorAlConstants, SuperstructureConstants, LEDConstants, AutoConstants, VisionConstants (incl. nested TrackingGains), and LoggingConstants. The 2025 Reefscape field tag IDs `REEF_TAGS = {6,7,8,9,10,11,17,18,19,20,21,22}` and `CORAL_STATION_TAGS = {1,2,12,13}` are declared identically in BOTH repos (A lines 405-406, B lines 191-192), as are `REEF_FLUSH_DISTANCE = 0.45`, `STATION_FLUSH_DISTANCE = 0.45`, and the entire `TrackingGains` block (DISTANCE_kP 1.5, ROTATION_kP 0.06, deadbands 0.05/1.0, clamps 2.0/1.0).
painPoints.libraryFix: Separate the axes: Rootstock owns field/game constants (tag classes, field dimensions) and default tracking gains; the robot repo owns only its hardware IDs and mechanism geometry. `LoggingConstants` (array index → component) should be replaced by a typed component-pose builder so index/CAD-order mismatch is impossible — currently it's three ints that must match a glTF export order documented in a separate README.

painPoints.problem: Tag-class membership is tested with hand-written linear scans over int arrays, duplicated per tag class per repo.
painPoints.evidence: A/Vision.java lines 131-147 and the identical block in B/Vision.java: `private static boolean isReefTag(int tagId) { for (int tag : VisionConstants.REEF_TAGS) { if (tag == tagId) return true; } return false; }` and the same again for `isCoralStationTag`. Four copies of the same loop across the two repos, running inside `findBestTarget()` on every camera on every 20 ms loop.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `TagClass` enum / `Set<Integer>` lookup in Rootstock's field model: `FieldTags.classOf(id)` returning REEF / CORAL_STATION / BARGE / PROCESSOR / UNKNOWN. Deletes four methods and makes 'which tags are trackable' a declarative table.

painPoints.problem: Manual velocity/output clamping is open-coded with nested Math.min/Math.max everywhere instead of a clamp helper.
painPoints.evidence: A/Swerve.java lines 412-414: `vx = Math.min(Math.max(vx, -MAX_LINEAR_VELOCITY), MAX_LINEAR_VELOCITY);` repeated three times in a row (duplicated identically in B/Swerve.java). Also A/Elevator.java:172 `targetPosition = Math.min(Math.max(targetPosition, MIN), MAX)`, A/Elevator.java:210, A/CorAl.java:191, B/AlLow.java:184, B/AlLow.java:213. Java 17 has no `Math.clamp` (added in 21), so every site re-nests.
painPoints.libraryFix: `RootstockMath.clamp(value, min, max)` and `deadband(value, band)` — trivial, but it removes ~10 error-prone nested expressions and gives one place to add logging/alerting when a command is being clamped (useful during tuning).

painPoints.problem: The elevator's manual control silently multiplies the stick by the speed limit AFTER deadbanding, and the deadband is applied in two different places for the same subsystem.
painPoints.evidence: A/RobotContainer.java lines 297-304 applies `ElevatorConstants.ELEVATOR_MANUAL_CONTROL_DEADBAND` in the default command, and then `Elevator.manualControl` (lines 207-210) applies the SAME deadband again plus the speed limit. CorAl and AlLow put the deadband only inside the subsystem — so the same team has two different conventions for the same concept across three mechanisms in two repos.
painPoints.libraryFix: A single `ManualControl` helper (deadband + scale + optional rate limit) owned by the library and applied in exactly one place, so 'where does the deadband live' stops being a per-mechanism decision.

painPoints.problem: Dead / vestigial logged state that will confuse anyone reading a log.
painPoints.evidence: A/RobotContainer.java lines 123-126 declares `@AutoLogOutput(key = "Draggables/DesiredComponents3d") public static Pose3d[] desiredComponents3d = {new Pose3d(), new Pose3d(), new Pose3d(), new Pose3d()};` — FOUR poses, never written anywhere, while the real `componentPoses` array in Dashboard has THREE. `@AutoLogOutput(key = "Draggables/FreshCode") public static boolean freshCode = true` is flipped once in `disabledExit()` with the comment `// The code isn't fresh anymore! - flaco`. Additionally `Dashboard.componentPoses` is BOTH `@AutoLogOutput(key="Draggables/Components3d")` and explicitly `Logger.recordOutput("RobotState/ComponentPoses", ...)` — the same array logged twice under two keys, and the advantageScopeAssets README references the `Draggables/` key while the main README references the `RobotState/` one.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `ComponentPoses` builder in Rootstock that owns the array, its length, its single log key, and the AdvantageScope config contract — so the number of components, the publish order, and the key can't disagree across three files (Constants.LoggingConstants, Dashboard, advantageScopeAssets/Robot_Leviathan/config.json).

painPoints.problem: Formatting is inconsistent within a single repo: tabs and 4-space indentation are mixed file-by-file, and the same file uses different indentation in the two repos.
painPoints.evidence: In A: Constants.java (354 tab-indented lines), TunerConstants.java (249 tabs), Robot.java (92 tabs), Swerve.java (401 tabs), Telemetry.java (92 tabs), Main.java (4 tabs) — but Dashboard.java (241 space lines), RobotContainer.java (253), CorAl.java (327), Elevator.java (209), LEDs.java (136), Vision.java (286), Superstructure.java (356) are all 4-space. TunerConstants.java is tab-indented in A and space-indented in B, which is why a naive diff reported 573 changed lines for a file with only ~15 real differences.
painPoints.libraryFix: Not a library API problem, but Rootstock should ship a formatter config (spotless/google-java-format or an .editorconfig) as part of the project template, so cross-robot diffs show real changes only. This directly reduces the cost of the copy-paste-between-robots workflow the team actually uses.

painPoints.problem: Committed simulation/dashboard scratch files and a stale generator project pollute the repos and actively mislead.
painPoints.evidence: A has `networktables.json`, `simgui.json`, `simgui-window.json`, `simgui-ds.json` committed at the repo root (B has only `simgui-ds.json`). `tuner-project.json` (Tuner X project) is committed in both and is documented as WRONG: A/TunerConstants.java header says 'NOTE: tuner-project.json (Tuner X project in the repo root) is STALE - it models all four modules as MK4n (18.75 steer) and holds different CANcoder offsets', and it does — tuner-project.json has FL EncoderOffset -0.07958984375 vs TunerConstants' -0.0888671875. The A README makes 'do not blindly regenerate TunerConstants from it' checklist item #1.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship a project template with a correct `.gitignore` (sim GUI state, build artifacts) and either exclude the Tuner project or provide a checked verification (a unit test asserting TunerConstants offsets match tuner-project.json, failing loudly when they drift) so a stale generator input can't silently produce a wrong regeneration.

painPoints.problem: Chassis characterization numbers are duplicated between Java and PathPlanner JSON with no cross-check, and are already inconsistent.
painPoints.evidence: B/TunerConstants.java line 82: `kSpeedAt12Volts = MetersPerSecond.of(5.96)` and stator limit `Amps.of(60)`. B/src/main/deploy/pathplanner/settings.json: `"maxDriveSpeed": 5.364`, `"driveCurrentLimit": 100.0`. A is self-consistent (5.96 / 90 in both), B is not — PathPlanner will plan trajectories against a top speed the code doesn't believe in. Both files also independently declare module positions (±0.314 m in JSON, `Inches.of(12.375)` = 0.3143 m in Java), wheel radius, gearing, and mass.
painPoints.libraryFix: One `ChassisConfig` in Rootstock as the source of truth, with a gradle task or unit test that validates `deploy/pathplanner/settings.json` against it. This is a silent-failure class of bug (auto just finishes off-target) that a library check catches for free.

painPoints.problem: Roller-stop safety is hand-applied per command instead of guaranteed by construction, and A's coral intake needed an explicit workaround for a rising-edge-only auto-stop.
painPoints.evidence: A/Superstructure.java has `.handleInterrupt(coral::stopIntake)` manually appended to `intakeCoral()`, `ejectCoral()`, and `scoreAlgae()` — with the comment `// Never leave rollers running on interrupt` repeated three times. `intakeCoral()` additionally needs an explicit `Commands.runOnce(coral::stopIntake, coral)` with a 5-line comment explaining that CorAl's periodic auto-stop only fires on the RISING edge, so a piece already latched before the rollers start would leave them running forever. Contrast B/KitBot.java, where `startEnd(..., motor::stopMotor)` makes this structurally impossible.
painPoints.libraryFix: Rootstock's `RollerSubsystem` should only expose command factories with stop-on-end built in (the KitBot shape), and a `GamePieceDetector` abstraction should expose a level signal (`isHeld()`) rather than only an edge, so 'run until held' works regardless of prior state.

painPoints.problem: Vision goal resolution — the one genuinely robot-specific part of Vision — is entangled with the copy-pasted 200 lines around it, forcing a full-file fork.
painPoints.evidence: The Vision.java diff between A and B is 99 lines, and every one of them is in the goal-resolver area: A has `BranchSide`, `setGoalSupplier(Supplier<Superstructure.Goal>)`, `tagMatchesCurrentGoal(int)` and a 13-line switch over `Superstructure.Goal`; B collapses all of it to `return Optional.of(new TrackingGoal(0.0, REEF_FLUSH_DISTANCE));` and filters with `if (getTrackingGoal(tagId).isEmpty()) continue;`. The other ~205 lines (MegaTag fusion, camera table name precomputation, `AprilTagTarget`, `toggleTracking`, caching) are identical.
painPoints.libraryFix: Make the goal resolver a first-class interface: `interface TrackingGoalResolver { Optional<TrackingGoal> resolve(int tagId); }`. Then B is a two-line lambda, A supplies its superstructure-aware implementation, and 205 lines of fusion/caching live in Rootstock. This is the cleanest seam in the entire survey.

constraints: Java 17 only — both repos pin `sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17`. No `Math.clamp` (Java 21), no records-in-patterns, no sealed-interface pattern matching. Rootstock must compile and run on 17.

Must work with GradleRIO 2026.2.1 / WPILib 2026 and the exact vendordep set already in use: Phoenix6 26.3.0, REVLib 2026.0.5, PathplannerLib 2026.1.2, AdvantageKit 26.0.2. Note GradleRIO 2026 hard-rejects vendordeps with a mismatched `frcYear` (this is why ChoreoLib is deliberately absent — documented in both READMEs).

Must not fight CTRE's Tuner-X-generated `TunerConstants.java` format. That file is regenerated by an external tool; Rootstock has to consume `SwerveDrivetrainConstants` + `SwerveModuleConstants<?,?,?>...` and extend `SwerveDrivetrain<TalonFX, TalonFX, CANcoder>` rather than replace it. The team already hand-edits it (per-module steer ratios for mixed MK4i/MK4n) so the library must tolerate hand-edited generated files.

Mixed-vendor hardware is mandatory, not optional: CTRE TalonFX/Kraken (swerve, A's CorAl) AND REV Spark MAX/NEO (A's elevator, B's KitBot + AlLow) in the same robot. Any motor abstraction must cover both, including their very different closed-loop idioms (Phoenix `MotionMagicVoltage` + `SensorToMechanismRatio` vs REVLib `kMAXMotionPositionControl` + `positionConversionFactor` + on-controller `FeedForwardConfig`).

Closed-loop control runs ON the motor controller, not the roboRIO, and the setpoint is expected to LATCH. This is a deliberate, repeatedly documented design choice ('The controller latches the setpoint; no need to re-send every loop'; 'the arm keeps holding its angle no matter which command is currently scheduled'). Rootstock must not impose a roboRIO-side periodic control loop that breaks the latch semantics — B's AlLowSimTest exists specifically as a regression net for it ('this was the original hold-position bug').

Motor configuration must persist to flash (`ResetMode.kResetSafeParameters, PersistMode.kPersistParameters` used everywhere) so a brownout can't revert controllers mid-match. Any config abstraction must preserve this.

Must not block the main loop on CAN. Explicitly encoded in A/CorAl.java: `pivotMotor.setPosition(x, 0)` with a zero timeout because 'the default setPosition overload BLOCKS the main loop waiting for the device ack (up to 100 ms)'. Similarly Vision uses `SetRobotOrientation_NoFlush` + one `LimelightHelpers.Flush()` per loop rather than per camera.

Vision timestamps must be converted FPGA→Phoenix (`Utils.fpgaToCurrentTime`) before reaching the CTRE pose estimator — hard requirement, documented as 'Passing raw FPGA time makes every measurement appear to be from the wrong moment and corrupts the pose estimate.'
Field-legal network ports only: 5800-5810. The layout WebServer takes 5800, so AdvantageKit's RLOGServer is pinned to 5810. A library that opens its own port must stay in that window and not collide.

AdvantageKit is used for LOGGING ONLY — no IO layers, no `@AutoLog` inputs classes, no deterministic replay. The A README states this explicitly: 'full AdvantageKit log replay would additionally require IO-layer hardware abstraction in every subsystem — not done here.' Rootstock should not force an IO-layer architecture on this team unless it's opt-in; their subsystems own hardware directly.

Dashboard target is Elastic (not Shuffleboard — 'Elastic dropped Shuffleboard API support'). Publishing must be plain NetworkTables under /SmartDashboard plus a `deploy/elastic-layout.json`, and the vendored `util/Elastic.java` (Gold87 ElasticLib) helper must keep working for `selectTab` and toast notifications.

Unit tests construct real (simulated) CAN devices, and vendor libs reject duplicate device IDs within one JVM — hence `forkEvery = 1` in build.gradle. Any library test utilities must survive that constraint.

Desktop simulation must keep working (`includeDesktopSupport = true`, `wpi.sim.addGui().defaultEnabled = true`). Known caveat to preserve/route around: REV's simulated MAXMotion advances on wall-clock time and mis-scales feedforward, which is why ElevatorSimTest deliberately does NOT assert a full profile move.

Gradle is pinned to the WPILib JDK via `org.gradle.java.home=C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026/jdk` because the machine's JAVA_HOME (Android Studio JBR) ships an msvcp140.dll that hard-crashes WPILib natives. Any build-template Rootstock ships must keep or document this escape hatch.

Team 9143 runs multiple robots simultaneously off one codebase lineage (A competition robot + B KitBot/practice robot). Rootstock must support per-robot divergence cleanly — different mechanisms, different auto gains (A: translation/rotation kP 5.0/5.0; B: 10.0/7.0), different CANcoder offsets, and a robot with ZERO cameras where the whole vision stack must stay inert without crashing (B guards its Y-binding with `if (VisionConstants.LIMELIGHT_NAMES.length > 0)`).
